4. The question now raised is whether the lower appellate court rightly decreed the suit when admittedly all the properties belonging to the plaintiffs and the defendants were not included in the hotchpotch of the partition suit. It appears that while the defendants obeying the non-inclusion of the joint properties referred to Khatian Number 25, 72 and 33. So far as Khatian No. 72 and 33 are concerned admittedly there was no community of interest between the plaintiffs and the defendants in the properties covered in such Khatians as have been found by both the courts below concurrently and consequently there was no cause for inclusion of any property covered by Khatian NO. 72 and 33 in the hotchpotch of the present partition suit which is now exclusively concerned with the khatian number 25 only. 

 5. So far as Khatian No. 25 is concerned it includes more than about 54 plots of lands out of which the plaintiffs have claimed partition with regard to six plots of lands only. For the rest of about 48 plots of lands not included in the hotchpotch of the partition suit, the plaintiffs alleged that these plots were already separately held between the plaintiffs and the defendants by virtue of a Deed of Gift executed and registered on 5.8.1933 at Jalpaigury now Within the State of West Bengal in India. The original copy, the registered deed of gift was allegedly and evidently lying with the defendant No. 1 as guardian of plaintiffs who were minors at the relevant time. A certified copy of the registered deed of gift issued by the Sub-Registrar of Jalpaigury was produced in court and attesting witnesses were examined in court in support of such deed- of gift. The certified copy of the Deed of Gift issued by the Sub-Registrar of Jalpaiguri in India was not however formally admitted in evidence because being a forged document it was not attested by any authority of the Government in the then East Pakistan. So far this registered deed of gift is concerned, it included all the plots of lands covered by Khatian No. 25 and it also allotted different plots of lands between the plaintiffs and defendants specifically while delivering the possession of such plots of lands to the plaintiffs and the defendants. The deed of gift however omitted specifically to allot six plots of lands within Khatian No. 25 between the plaintiffs and the defendants and these omissions in the deed of gift caused the plaintiffs to institute the present partition suit for the allocation of the remaining six plots of lands in Khatian No. 25 between the plaintiffs and the defendants. 

 6. From the foregoing facts and circumstances of the case it, would clearly appear that it is an admitted fact and concurrently held by both the courts below that the plaintiffs and the defendants were separately, possessing all the plots of lands covered by khatian: No. 25 excepting the present six plots of lands by virtue of the deed of gift registered and executed Jalpaiguri on 5.8.33. That apart from the remaining six plots of lands in khatian. No. 25, all other plots of lands were held by the plaintiffs and the defendants separately as mentioned in the registered deed of gift when admittedly the plaintiffs and defendants were possessing their respective plots of lands separately excepting the present six plots of lands within khatian No. 25. There was no occasion for either the plaintiffs or the defendants to cause any partition of such plots of lands which were held and possessed separately by the plaintiffs and the defendants. The present cause of action for instituting the present partition suit arose be-cause six plots of lands within khatian No. 25 were not allotted separately to the plaintiffs and the defendants. In such circumstances the question is whether, it. could be called a partial partition if at all, and if so; whether such partial partition could be allowed in the present facts and circumstances of the case for ends of justice and equity. 

 7. When, admittedly the plaintiffs and the defendants were holding all other plots of lands exempting six plots of lands in khatian No. 25, it must be presumed that there was an amicabla partition between the parties by virtue of the registered deed of gift. Since six plots of Iands in Khatian No. 25 were not specifically allotted to the plaintiff and the defendants in the registered deed of gift the parties had to hold and possess such lands jointly by compulsion. The general rule is that a suit for partition shall include the entire properties of the co-sharers held and possessed jointly but in the present case it cannot be said that all the plots of lands in khatian No. 25 were held and possessed jointly by the plaintiffs and the defendants since excepting six plots of lands and all other plots of lands were held and possessed by the plaintiffs and the defendants separately. Only with regard to six plots of lands the plaintiffs and the defendants are holding and possessing such properties jointly as, co-sharers. It must be observed that the general rule to include the entire properties of all the co-sharers held and possessed jointly in a suit for partition is a rule of equity and which could be relaxed when a partition might be necessary for ends of justice and without causing any prejudice to any party. A rule of equity as opposed to a rule of law shall be applied on the convenience of the parties concerned and may be relaxed from time to time for ends of justice in the interest of the parties concerned without causing prejudice to anyone. This view was taken by Mr. Justice Ibrahim in a decision reported in 5 D.L.R. at page 511. In the present case when evidently there is no occasion to include all the plots of lands covered by Khatian No. 25 within the hotchpotch of the partition suit since excepting the present disputed six plots of lands all other plots of lands were held and possessed by the plaintiffs and the defendants separately, there was valid reason for the plaintiffs to sue for partition only with regard to six plots of lands admittedly held and possessed jointly by the plaintiff and the defendants. 

 8. In the foregoing facts and circumstances of the case stated hereinbefore, the lower appellate court rightly decreed the plaintiff’s suit for partition against the defendants with regard to six plots of lands in khatian No. 25 between the plaintiffs and the defendants. There is no illegality in the judgment and of the lower appellant’s court and consequently this appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.
